issues: suspected_loci includes torsional_coordinates, which is not shown in the inventory
reverse_invariance probe uses graph.ts_reverse, while the inventory only shows graph.ts.reverse as the public reverse API
probe graphs do not specify implicit hydrogen counts, so some constructed automol graphs may be invalid
suggested_fixes: Replace or verify torsional_coordinates with a rotor-coordinate function actually present in source/automol/graph/base/ts.py
Use graph.ts.reverse in the reverse_invariance probe, or import the exact public name shown in the workflow
Construct probe graphs with explicit atm_imp_hyd_dct or another validated public constructor to guarantee valid molecular graphs

issues: Several probes build hypervalent graphs by adding explicit H atoms while also setting 3 implicit hydrogens on the same carbons.
The ethane-like TS may have no rotatable coordinate if the only C-C bond is a fractional TS bond, so relabel/reverse probes can pass vacuously.
connectivity_change removes the only C-C bond, producing disconnected/hypervalent fragments that may not be supported by rotational_coordinates.
Invariance probes do not assert a nonempty signature before comparing presentations.
suggested_fixes: Use valid graphs: set implicit hydrogens to 0 where H atoms are explicit, or use implicit hydrogens only, and ensure the TS has a real rotatable single bond such as a butane-like backbone.
Add a nonempty-coordinate or nonempty-signature assertion to relabel_invariance and reverse_invariance before comparing signatures.
Make the connectivity-change probe modify a connected graph, for example by changing a bond order or removing a non-essential bond, instead of disconnecting it.
Replace random relabeling with a fixed permutation for deterministic probes.
